clue.text: Motivated university Head of Physics after everyone gets sacked

parts.note: everyone means all
sacked from a job is fired
U is the standard abbreviation for university

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of the next word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Physics

explanation.surface: A university physics head is thrilled once all the staff have been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the university-and-physics letters come after the everyone-sacked part.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fired up is eager and energised, so the phrase is an idiom for being keen and driven.

clue.text: Fat, heartless Scottish landowner

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the following word is taken away

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish estate owner

explanation.surface: An insult aimed at a portly Scottish landowner who also lacks compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: LAIRD loses its middle letter I to leave LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Identify good, more exquisite clothes

indicators.note: used as a verb, clothes means dresses or wraps around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: more exquisite means finer
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Choosing between good and even more exquisite garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun about garments but is a verb: FINER wraps round G.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger someone is slang for pointing them out to the police, informally naming or picking out a culprit.

clue.text: One of the strings pulled to get on in the Parachute Regiment?

definitions.text: One of the strings pulled to get on in the Parachute Regiment?

parts.words: One of the strings pulled to get on
parts.note: surface reading: pulling strings, using influence to get ahead in one's career
setter's reading: a literal cord a paratrooper pulls to open the canopy and carry on safely down

explanation.surface: Someone using connections to win promotion in the Paras.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulling strings is an idiom for using influence; here the string is real, the cord that opens a parachute.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripcord is the cord pulled to release a parachute from its pack.

clue.text: Sailor under the doctor, looking bleak

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something means coming below it, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor being treated by the doctor and looking miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dull and cheerless in appearance, matching a bleak look.

clue.text: Throw out work assignment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to cast or thrust forward
second meaning: a noun, a planned piece of work set for someone

explanation.surface: Rejecting a task you were handed at work.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to hurl or cast forward; as a noun it is a planned undertaking or task.

clue.text: Junk (tandem) rows with the current

indicators.note: to junk something is to scrap it, so these letters are broken up and remade

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Chinese junk crewed by rowers pulling in tandem, going along with the flow.
explanation.walkthrough: Junk looks like the boat in the picture but is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Going downstream means travelling in the direction a river flows, along with its current.

clue.text: Boy and unknown man clear out episcopal place of worship

parts.note: a boy is a lad
Y is a mathematical unknown
chap is informal for man

indicators.note: clearing out the inside of a word empties it, so only its outermost letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of episcopal

explanation.surface: A boy and a stranger clearing out a bishop's church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Episcopal place of worship' reads as one phrase, but episcopal is only the source of two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lady Chapel is a chapel dedicated to the Virgin Mary within a larger church, so a place for prayer.

clue.text: Spanish master returning banana yogurt pots

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the concealed letters are read from right to left
to pot is to hold in a container, so the words that follow hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the end of banana and the start of yogurt run together

explanation.surface: A Spanish chef coming back to pot up banana yogurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a celebrated Spanish painter, and an old master is a great painter of earlier centuries.

clue.text: Joanna, Pandora getting sozzled with gin

indicators.note: sozzled means very drunk, and drunk things lurch about out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two women, Joanna and Pandora, getting drunk on gin.
explanation.walkthrough: Joanna looks like a woman's name but is Cockney rhyming slang: joanna rhymes with piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Joanna is rhyming slang for a piano, and a grand is the large horizontal concert kind.

clue.text: Sprightly corvid eating nut excitedly

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the jay is a member of the crow family

indicators.note: something done excitedly is agitated and jumbled, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crow-family bird happily pecking at a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: Corvid is the family name for crows, jays, magpies and rooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaunty describes a lively, cheerful and self-confident manner, much like sprightly.

clue.text: Ordinary retired clergyman discovering barmy bowling technique

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the clergyman's title is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

indicators.note: dis-covering means taking the cover off, so the outer letters are stripped away leaving the middle

parts.note: barmy without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An ordinary retired vicar finding a crazy way to bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovering' seems to mean finding, but split as dis-covering it means removing the cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Overarm bowling, with the arm swung above the shoulder, is the standard delivery action in cricket.

clue.text: Fan of cable broadcast is unstable

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cable-TV enthusiast whose favourite channel is shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off balance means wobbly and liable to fall, the physical sense of lacking steadiness.

clue.text: Mopes around depressed Southern Railway station for Derby

indicators.note: turned around signals the letters are moved about into another order

parts.note: taken as written
depressed means down
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Someone moping about a gloomy station on the Southern Railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: Southern Railway reads as a train company, but it splits: S from Southern, Railway starts the definition. The Derby is the famous horse race run on the Downs at Epsom in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a station in Surrey serving the racecourse where the Derby is held each summer.

clue.text: Gong finally sounded during Dinner for One

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the letter sits inside the other piece

parts.note: dinner is one example of a meal

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word beside it

parts.note: the closing letter of sounded

explanation.surface: A dinner gong sounding at the end of a table-for-one meal; Dinner for One is also a famous comic sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' means 'for example': dinner is an instance of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or decoration, as in an honour from the Queen.

clue.text: Nick caught vermin in school

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so these pieces go within the school

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a rat is vermin

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick caught a rat in the school building.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a man's name but is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick and a scratch are both small superficial cuts or marks on a surface.

clue.text: Ground spice put into tiramisu macaroons

indicators.note: something put into the dessert is sitting inside those words, concealed across them

parts.note: the tail of tiramisu joined to the start of macaroons

explanation.surface: A recipe step: sprinkle ground spice into the tiramisu and macaroons.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a tangy red Middle Eastern seasoning made by grinding the dried berries of a shrub.

clue.text: Went by Underground (westbound) for the first time

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in a debut album, one appearing for the first time

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means travelling right to left, the opposite way to normal reading

parts.note: the London Underground is the Tube, so travelling by it is tubed

explanation.surface: A first-ever ride on the London Underground heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: The Underground is London's metro, nicknamed the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A debut is a first appearance, so the word describes something happening or performed initially.

clue.text: Secure quickly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: firmly fixed, as in held tight

explanation.definitionFit: The word means firmly fixed, as in stuck tight, and also rapidly, as in running at speed.

clue.text: Succour pup losing weight

indicators.note: losing means giving something up, so a letter drops out of the word

parts.note: a whelp is a puppy
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: Caring for a puppy that is losing weight.
explanation.walkthrough: WHELP without its W leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour means aid or assistance given to someone in need.

clue.text: Lacquer, usually Black Country

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hard glossy varnish, typically black
second meaning: the East Asian nation

explanation.surface: Black Country lacquer, as if from the industrial West Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Country is an industrial area of the English West Midlands, but here Black and Country belong to different meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a glossy black varnish named after the lacquerware of that island nation, which is also an Asian state.

clue.text: Sailor departs area with flighty thief

parts.note: jack, as in Jack Tar, is a sailor
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
A is the abbreviation for area
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A sailor runs off with a fickle crook.
explanation.walkthrough: Flighty suggests fickle but literally means able to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a small crow famous for snatching shiny objects, so a winged robber.

clue.text: Arrest fine, very old revolutionary writer

parts.note: to nab is to arrest
OK means fine

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning round, so the last two letters are turned back to front

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Police arrest and fine an elderly radical author.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American novelist who wrote Lolita and Pale Fire.

clue.text: Senior sailor making a mark in Dead Sea?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the mark goes into the sea

parts.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia has largely dried up, so it is a dead sea
DM is the abbreviation for the Deutschmark
a means one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A senior naval officer leaving his mark on the Dead Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A mark' means one Deutschmark, the old German currency, with the one written as a Roman numeral after the currency symbol. The Dead Sea of the surface is not the sea used; the question mark flags a dead sea, one that has dried up.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is the highest-ranking officer in a navy, so the most senior seafarer.

clue.text: Golden brown mare running in The Golden State?

indicators.note: in means sitting inside, so the mixed letters go within the state

parts.note: California is nicknamed the Golden State; CAL is a short form

indicators.note: something running is in motion, so these letters move about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A golden-brown horse galloping in California.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is the warm yellowish-brown colour of melted burnt sugar.

clue.text: American soft fruit crop up

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
P, piano, is the musical notation for soft
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: An American soft-fruit harvest coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit crop' looks like a harvest, but crop belongs with up.
explanation.definitionFit: To crop up is to arise or turn up unexpectedly, which is to show oneself or emerge.

clue.text: Geeky individual in waterproof clothing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for an obsessive enthusiast
second meaning: a hooded weatherproof jacket

explanation.surface: A nerd dressed in a rain jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an anorak is a nerdy obsessive, from the jackets worn by trainspotters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a hooded weatherproof jacket and, by association with train spotters, an obsessive hobbyist.

clue.text: Prey of female bird of prey?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
an owl is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: Wondering what a hen hawk or she-owl might hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: poultry is what a raptor might catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Fowl, game birds and poultry, are among the creatures hunted and eaten by predators.

clue.text: Fine summer in Paris for a garden party

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
French for summer is été

explanation.surface: Fine summer weather in Paris, ideal for an outdoor party.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fundraising event with stalls and games, typically held on a lawn.

clue.text: Bouncer rejecting rude-sounding goalie

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so the letters run the other way
sounding means as heard spoken, so the word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: rood, a cross, is pronounced like rude
a goalie is a goalkeeper

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer turning away a goalkeeper who sounds rude.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouncer suggests a nightclub heavy, a sense that does fit the doorman role here.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer guards an entrance, deciding who comes in, which is the job of a person posted at a door.

clue.text: Tory Kelvin is a snitch

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
K is the symbol for kelvin

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician called Kelvin turns informer.
explanation.walkthrough: Snitch here is old British slang for the nose, not an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal slang words for the nose.

clue.text: Very knowledgeable on source of water freshly served

parts.note: a well is a source of water

indicators.note: freshly means anew, so these letters are made up again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An expert on spring water that has just been poured.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well-versed in a subject means being thoroughly experienced and informed about it.
